name: Chandra
summary: The yakshi heroine of Lokah Chapter 1: Chandra (2025), Malayalam cinema's first 300 crore film and the start of a folklore-based superhero universe.
origin: Chandra is a yakshi who lives quietly as a young woman in Bengaluru. She is a reimagining of Kalliyankattu Neeli, a yakshi of Kerala folk songs and tales. In the film's own telling, Neeli was a tribal girl whose village was destroyed, who gained supernatural powers after a bat bite and avenged her parents. The story brings her into a world of Chathans, Odiyans and a sorcerer-priest, with the elder Moothon as the shadow looming over them.
powers: Abilities tied to a bat-bite origin in the film's telling

storyline.title: Kalliyankattu Neeli
storyline.beat: The film builds on the Kerala folk figure of Neeli, giving her its own origin of a tribal girl who gained powers after a bat bite and avenged her family.

storyline.title: A yakshi in Bengaluru
storyline.beat: Chandra works and lives unnoticed in a modern city while Chathans, Odiyans and corrupt men circle her neighbourhood.

storyline.title: A record run
storyline.beat: The film opens modestly, then becomes the first Malayalam release to pass 300 crore worldwide and holds the all-time record until Bethlehem Kudumba Unit (2026).

storyline.title: More chapters
storyline.beat: Lokah Chapter 2 was announced with Tovino Thomas in the lead, as part of a planned multi-film universe.

gossip.text: Chandra is also known by the folklore name Kalliyankattu Neeli.
Wikipedia lists Lokah among the highest-grossing Indian films with a female lead, and a 2026 Malayalam film later passed its all-time record.
Dulquer Salmaan appears only in a cameo, even though he produced the film and had wanted it made without him acting.
In the film, a book credited to the pen name Joseph Dominic records the supernatural beings who live among humans, and the story compares it to the old Kerala folklore collection Aithihyamala.
Dulquer hopes his father Mammootty will play Moothon in a future chapter, but says the team must first earn his trust.

quiz.q: What kind of being is Chandra in Kerala folklore?
quiz.why: Chandra is a yakshi, a female nature spirit in Kerala folklore.

quiz.q: Which Malayalam milestone did Lokah Chapter 1 reach?
quiz.why: It was the first Malayalam film to cross Rs 300 crore worldwide.
Dominic Arun wrote and directed it.

quiz.q: Which actor plays Chandra in Lokah Chapter 1?
quiz.why: Kalyani Priyadarshan plays Chandra in the title role.

quiz.q: What burns Chandra's skin in the film?
quiz.why: The film names sunlight as one of Chandra's weaknesses.

timeline.title: Theatrical release
timeline.note: Lokah Chapter 1: Chandra opens on 28 August 2025 in Malayalam, with dubs soon after.

timeline.title: Chapter 2 announced

timeline.note: About six weeks after release it becomes the first Malayalam film above Rs 300 crore worldwide.

timeline.note: Bethlehem Kudumba Unit takes the all-time Malayalam box-office record that Lokah held.

facts.text: It began as a small indie about Neeli, a yakshi, then grew to bring in a Chathan (wizard), an Odiyan (shapeshifter) and a Kathanar (sorcerer) from Kerala lore.

Kalliyankattu Neeli is a yakshi from Kerala folk songs, Villadichan songs and C. V. Raman Pillai's 1891 novel Marthandavarma; at the Parumala Valiya Panayannarkavu temple she has a shrine where devotees offer black glass bangles.

In the film's telling, Neeli was a tribal girl whose village a caste-enforcing king destroyed; a bat bite gave her powers, she avenged her parents, and Kadamattathu Kathanar then recruited her for Moothon.
Chandra is summoned from Sweden to Bengaluru by Prakash, Moothon's helper; the call really comes from Moothon, 'the Elder', a mysterious figure.
Naslen plays Sunny, Chandra's neighbour and the film's other lead, and also Michael Joseph, a British soldier of 1905 who looks just like Sunny and was Chandra's love interest, seen in a photograph.
Chandra's weak points in the film are sunlight, which burns her skin, and her heart, which can be fatal; she heals by drinking packed blood supplied to her.
Her bite changes only healthy people into yakshas; the film explains that anyone else dies of a rabies-like illness.
Director Arun told Kalyani Priyadarshan that Chandra must not move the way Kalyani normally does; Kalyani says she found a way to glide as if floating through time and space.
The mid-credits scene reveals Charlie, an Odiyan, played in a cameo by producer Dulquer Salmaan himself.
The post-credits scene has Michael asked about vanished archaeologists; he says a photo shows one of his 389 siblings.
Estimates put the budget at about Rs 30 to 40 crore, yet the film went on to earn over Rs 300 crore worldwide.
Moothon never appears in person: his voice is Mammootty's, and the camera shows only an arm to stand for him.
The film's Bengaluru setting and its Rear Window-style shots salute Vandanam (1989), directed by Priyadarshan, who is Kalyani's father.
In some Kerala tellings the priest-magician Kadamattathu Kathanar ritually binds Neeli to a stone, which makes the surrounding forest safe again.
One folk strand has Neeli reborn as a Chola king's child, along with a brother, Neelan; the king abandons them in a forest, and a ritual expert can destroy Neelan but cannot stop Neeli.
Neeli was on screen long before Lokah: a 1979 Malayalam horror film, Kalliyankattu Neeli, made her its lead, and she also appears in the 1984 film Kadamattathachan.
Asked to do the cameo, producer Dulquer Salmaan's first thought was that the team should be able to make the film without him, and he joked about how odd it was to produce his own superhero movie.
Salmaan says Kalyani's father, the director Priyadarshan, phoned him to ask what he had been thinking when he made such a big bet; Mammootty is said to have worried about the rising costs.
Arun and cinematographer Nimish Ravi first planned an indie-style film within a budget thought affordable for a female-led story; Salmaan told them to think beyond those limits.
Some lines spoken by Inspector Nachiyappa Gowda caused outrage in Bengaluru for painting its residents unfairly, and the producer, Wayfarer Films, issued an open apology.
The old storyteller Verghese Kurien turns out to be the book's author, Joseph Dominic, and Chandra is revealed to be Neeli herself, now immortal.
When police shoot Chandra, she is rescued by Michael, a Chathan who lives quietly as a street magician and uses illusions to beat the officers.
Lokah opened to only about Rs 6.66 crore worldwide, yet went on to become the first Malayalam film past Rs 300 crore, about six weeks after release.

kidSummary: Chandra is a young woman from Kerala folk tales who looks ordinary but is really a yakshi with special powers. In the film she lives in a big city and protects her neighbours from trouble.

story.title: An old folk tale
story.text: Kerala tales tell of Kalliyankattu Neeli, a girl with special powers. The film brings her into today's world.

story.title: A quiet life
story.text: Chandra lives in a big city, hiding her powers and doing everyday things like anyone else.

story.title: A call from Moothon
story.text: A mysterious elder called Moothon sends for Chandra, and she meets other beings from Kerala lore.

story.title: Trouble in the neighbourhood
story.text: A corrupt policeman threatens the people she cares about, and Chandra uses her strength to protect them.

story.title: More chapters to come
story.text: After the first film, the makers announced more chapters set in the same world of folk-tale heroes.
